youtube.title: Can a Crow Raise Food with Stones? | Toxic Tales
youtube.description:
Could a trained crow raise a floating reward with stones? Six New Caledonian crows made choices between materials and water-filled tubes. They more often used water than sand, sinking rather than floating objects, and solid rather than hollow ones. They favoured higher starting water—but did not reliably prefer the more efficient narrow tube or identify a concealed functional U-tube connection. Only four birds completed every test. These controlled tasks show selectivity, not proof of complete causal understanding or of wild stone-dropping.

Jelbert et al. (2014), PLOS ONE 9(3):e92895. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0092895
Full open-access paper: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3966847/
Evidence, limitations and credits: https://akshaymohan16.github.io/toxic-tales-library/sources/tt-010.html
